sources_considered.why: Primary survey explicitly asks non-users why they do not use generative AI; fieldwork occurred in fall and winter 2024.
Dated institutional announcement establishes that the report was publicly available by March 9, 2025.
Original R1 report compares reasoning performance with an existing model, but does not establish exhaustive functional equivalence.
Describes performance and training improvements, without an exhaustive comparison of user-facing functionality.
Describes Janus-Pro improvements, but does not establish whether they constituted new functionality relative to all alternatives.
read_page returned current API instructions rather than the historical announcement.

evidence_items.publisher: Harry C. Katz and Mark D. Gough / National Academy of Arbitrators
evidence_items.explanation: In the 2024 survey, some professional non-users identified cost as influencing non-adoption. March 9 is a conservative public-availability date established by Cornell's announcement of the February report, not a claimed exact first-publication date.

This supports the narrower point that R1 addressed reasoning tasks already served by another model. Comparable benchmark performance does not prove that every user-facing function was already available elsewhere.

unresolved_gaps: The survey does not isolate API prices or establish that cost was the sole reason for non-adoption.
Professional non-adoption does not necessarily mean respondents had never experimented privately.
No exhaustive contemporary feature comparison establishes the full absence of new DeepSeek functionality.
